subject: gk
question: Article 51 of Directive Principles of State Policy enumerates which of the following ?

options.text: Promotion of international peace and security
Uniform civil code for the citizens
Organisation of agricultural and animal husbandry

solution:
The correct answer is __**Promotion of international peace and security**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Article 51 of the Directive Principles of State Policy directs the state to promote international peace and security.

• It emphasizes the importance of maintaining just and honorable relations between nations.

• The article also advocates for respect for international law and treaty obligations.

• It encourages settlement of international disputes by arbitration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**

• The Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government. These provisions are contained in Part IV (Article 36 to 51) of the Indian Constitution.

• They are non-justiciable in nature, which means they are not enforceable by the courts for their violation.

• However, they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country, intended to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.

• The DPSPs aim to establish a welfare state by securing and protecting social order, promoting the welfare of the people, and reducing inequalities in income, status, and opportunities.

• **Separation of judiciary from executive**

• Article 50 of the Indian Constitution directs the state to take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State.

• This principle aims to ensure the independence of the judiciary and prevent any influence of the executive on judicial decisions.

• **Uniform civil code for the citizens**

• Article 44 of the Indian Constitution directs the state to endeavor to secure a Uniform Civil Code for all citizens, which would replace the system of fragmented personal laws based on religious scriptures and customs.

• The goal of this provision is to ensure equality and justice for all citizens irrespective of their religion.

• **Organisation of agricultural and animal husbandry**

• Article 48 of the Indian Constitution directs the state to organize agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines.

• It also includes steps for preserving and improving the breeds and prohibiting the slaughter of cows and calves and other milch and draught cattle.
